title: Mathilde Bruguet
text:
I have been a doctoral student in statistics since November 2024 at IRMAR, under the supervision of David Causeur, Nadia Ponts and Gaël Le Trionaire.
My research focuses on the mixtures of regression models in a Gaussian framework and more specifically, in the context of a multi-view approach, that is to say within different groups. My research is applied to the analysis of epigenetic data, in order to determine models of associations between chromatin accessibility and gene expression. More specifically, the multi-view approach makes it possible to determine differences from one group to another. These approaches are based on the model of Fusarium graminearum, a wheat phytopathogenic organism whose virulence is supposed to increase due to environmental change via epigenetic mechanisms. The study of these mechanisms upstream is therefore essential to understanding this organism with significant economic impacts on wheat. Graduated from the Institut Agro Rennes - Angers, I completed a specialization in Data Science at the end of my studies as an Engineer in Horticulture. Statistical approaches now allow me to carry out analyses specific to biology and specifically to genomics, a field I have studied extensively, particularly in plants and their pests and pests.
Currently in the final year of my thesis, I am pursuing an academic career.
